_readme: W-0203 / P1.2. The API half of the LocalMockE2E profile.
Small on purpose. The API places no calls and runs no loops, so almost nothing about the
rehearsal belongs here; it exists so that a shell which exports IVR_CONFIG_PROFILE for the
whole stack starts the API rather than failing to find a file, and so the intake side of the
MOCK dial-token vault is configured from the same place as the dispatch side.
The token mapping matters more than it looks. MockDialTokenVault.Protect runs at INTAKE, in
this process, and MockDialTokenVault.ResolveAsync runs at DISPATCH, in the worker - separate
deployables with separate memory. The wildcard is what makes the two halves agree on a fake
destination without either of them ever holding a phone number.
Logging drops to Warning because the API logs every EF command at Information, and a hundred
rounds of that buries the one line a rehearsal exists to print.
W-0354 / C15. Ivr:Scheduler:CallingWindow is widened to the whole day here as in the worker's
profile. Since W-0298 the API refuses a task at intake that falls outside calling hours (since B17,
2026-09-25: one whose window opens outside them), so without this a rehearsal started after
21:08 - or a four-hour soak that runs past it - has every task refused at the door with
CALLING_WINDOW_CLOSED_FOR_WHOLE_CONFIRMATION_WINDOW.
W-0356 / K-04. MockChannelCount and ExpectedCallDurationSeconds copy the worker's profile.
Eligibility runs in this process and sizes capacity with exactly these two values; left at the
defaults (1 channel, 60 s a call) it judged a rehearsal against a pool far smaller than the one
the worker dials with. The worker's loop keys (Enabled, polling, leases) stay out: the API runs
no scheduler loop.
